name: Target State
description: 10-slide target-state deck for an engagement. Engine fills cover + cross-section metadata; AI writes the forces narrative (drivers from findings + risks), the target-state architecture narrative, the recommendation shaping prose, and the transition-risks summary.

sections.title: Findings driving the target state
sections.purpose: 3–5 markdown bullets summarising the most material findings that motivate moving to a new target state. Tight, business-readable language. No `[severity/domain]` prefixes — describe the issue and its consequence.

sections.title: Risks driving the target state
sections.purpose: 3–5 markdown bullets covering the risks that justify the target-state move. Each bullet: the risk, the materiality, and the strategic angle (why fixing this requires architecture change, not just process). No prefixes.

sections.title: Target-state architecture narrative
sections.purpose: 3–5 sentences describing the proposed target architecture at a strategic level: what shape it takes, the key technology/operating-model shifts, and how it addresses the forces on the prior slide. Prose, not bullets. No raw component lists — this is a narrative for leadership.

sections.title: Recommendations shaping the target
sections.purpose: 4–6 markdown bullets capturing the top recommendations that physically shape this target state (architecture, platform, process). Skip purely operational/team-level recs. Each bullet: outcome-oriented, not task-oriented.

sections.title: Transition risks
sections.purpose: 3–5 markdown bullets describing the 'risks of moving' — distinct from the steady-state risks shown on slide 3. These are the things that can go wrong while migrating: cutover failures, dual-running burden, dependency staging. Each bullet: the risk + one phrase on mitigation.
